notes: Destinations for which EEI must be filed whatever the value, so the $2,500 exemption (15 CFR 30.37(a)) never applies and an ITN is always required. Derived from 15 CFR 758.1(b)(1) (EEI regardless of value for Country Group E:1 and E:2) and Supplement No. 1 to 15 CFR part 740 (the Country Group E table). 15 CFR Part 30 itself names no country: 30.2(a)(1)(iv) lists license-required shipments, not destinations. To re-check, read both eCFR sections and compare the Country Group E table with `destinations`; the list changes when BIS amends that table (for example when a country is removed from E:1). Deliberately NOT listed: PRC/Hong Kong, Russia and Venezuela (758.1(b)(10) covers Commerce Control List items only, so it depends on the product, not the destination); Canada (30.36 exempts it, the opposite direction); license-required and other item-based rules in 30.2(a)(1)(iv) and 758.1(b)(2)-(9) and (11), which depend on the goods and cannot be decided from the destination. Read via https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-10-06/title-15.xml?part=30 (also part=758 and part=740).
derived_from: 15 CFR Supplement No. 1 to Part 740 (Country Group E)

CU.name: Cuba
CU.source: 15 CFR 758.1(b)(1): "For all exports of items subject to the EAR that are destined to a country in Country Group E:1 or E:2 of supplement no. 1 to part 740 of the EAR regardless of value". Supplement No. 1 to Part 740 lists Cuba in Country Group E:2 (Unilateral embargo). 15 CFR 30.37 opens "Except as noted in § 30.2(a)(1)(iv)", so the 30.37(a) $2,500 exemption does not rescue it. Read from the eCFR API, title 15 as of 2026-10-06.
